```{r Step 1, include=TRUE}
# ============================================================
# Presidential Voting, Employment Quality, and
# Economic Dispossession
#
# Elections:
#   2004, 2008, 2012, 2016, 2020, 2024
#
# Primary outcome:
#   Voting for the presidential candidate of the
#   respondent's out-party
#
# Main predictors:
#   compensation
#   benefits
#   earnings_stability
#   jqi_primary
#   prestige
#   realrinc / log_realrinc
#   financial_satisfaction
#
# Main controls:
#   wrkstat_factor
#   social_class_factor
#   polviews_factor
#   party_factor
#   age
#   sex_factor
#   education
#
# NOTE:
# The first stage uses conventional respondent-level SEs.
# A separate supplementary script will address industry-year
# assignment and clustered/assignment-aware inference.
# ============================================================


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. Packages
# ------------------------------------------------------------

library(tidyverse)
library(haven)
library(broom)
library(lmtest)
library(sandwich)
library(here)
library(gssr)
library(gssrdoc)

# Use MASS::polr explicitly elsewhere if needed.
# Do NOT library(MASS), to avoid masking dplyr::select().


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load / prepare the GSS data
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# This assumes gss_all is already your broader cross-sectional
# GSS file containing the presidential vote variables.
#
# If it is not currently loaded:
#
data("gss_all")



# Check the presidential variables before recoding.
pres_vars <- c(
  "pres04",
  "pres08",
  "pres12",
  "pres16",
  "pres20",
  "whovote24"
)

gss_all %>%
  dplyr::select(year, all_of(pres_vars)) %>%
  summarise(
    across(
      everything(),
      ~ n_distinct(.x, na.rm = TRUE)
    )
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Inspect presidential vote coding
# ------------------------------------------------------------
#
# IMPORTANT:
# We are deliberately inspecting the labels rather than
# assuming numeric coding.
#
# Run this section first and examine the output.

for (v in pres_vars) {

  cat("\n\n============================\n")
  cat(v, "\n")
  cat("============================\n")

  print(
    gss_all %>%
      dplyr::filter(!is.na(.data[[v]])) %>%
      dplyr::count(
        vote_raw = haven::as_factor(.data[[v]], levels = "labels"),
        sort = TRUE
      )
  )
}



# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Function to mechanically classify presidential vote
# ------------------------------------------------------------
#
# We identify the named Democratic and Republican candidate
# using the GSS value labels.
#
# Third-party candidates and non-voters are coded NA.
#
# This avoids relying on numeric coding that may differ
# across election years.

classify_pres_vote <- function(x, election_year) {

  x_label <- haven::as_factor(x, levels = "labels") %>%
    as.character() %>%
    stringr::str_to_lower()

  dem_pattern <- switch(
    as.character(election_year),

    "2004" = "kerry",
    "2008" = "obama",
    "2012" = "obama",
    "2016" = "clinton",
    "2020" = "biden",
    "2024" = "harris",

    stop("Election year not recognized.")
  )

  rep_pattern <- switch(
    as.character(election_year),

    "2004" = "bush",
    "2008" = "mccain",
    "2012" = "romney",
    "2016" = "trump",
    "2020" = "trump",
    "2024" = "trump",

    stop("Election year not recognized.")
  )

  case_when(
    stringr::str_detect(x_label, dem_pattern) ~ "Democratic",
    stringr::str_detect(x_label, rep_pattern) ~ "Republican",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  )
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Build election-specific presidential vote variables
# ------------------------------------------------------------

gss_vote <- gss_all %>%
  mutate(

    # 2004: Bush vs Kerry
    vote_2004 = case_when(
      haven::as_factor(pres04, levels = "labels") == "bush" ~
        "Republican",
      haven::as_factor(pres04, levels = "labels") == "kerry" ~
        "Democratic",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    # 2008: Obama vs McCain
    vote_2008 = case_when(
      haven::as_factor(pres08, levels = "labels") == "obama" ~
        "Democratic",
      haven::as_factor(pres08, levels = "labels") == "mccain" ~
        "Republican",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    # 2012: Obama vs Romney
    vote_2012 = case_when(
      haven::as_factor(pres12, levels = "labels") == "obama" ~
        "Democratic",
      haven::as_factor(pres12, levels = "labels") == "romney" ~
        "Republican",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    # 2016: Clinton vs Trump
    vote_2016 = case_when(
      haven::as_factor(pres16, levels = "labels") == "clinton" ~
        "Democratic",
      haven::as_factor(pres16, levels = "labels") == "trump" ~
        "Republican",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    # 2020: Biden vs Trump
    vote_2020 = case_when(
      haven::as_factor(pres20, levels = "labels") == "biden" ~
        "Democratic",
      haven::as_factor(pres20, levels = "labels") == "trump" ~
        "Republican",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    # 2024: GSS vote intention
    #
    # IMPORTANT: whovote24 is an intention measure.
    # The GSS labels show Joe Biden rather than Harris.
    vote_2024 = case_when(
      haven::as_factor(whovote24, levels = "labels") ==
        "joe biden" ~
        "Democratic",
      haven::as_factor(whovote24, levels = "labels") ==
        "donald trump" ~
        "Republican",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )

  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Party identification
# ------------------------------------------------------------

gss_vote <- gss_vote %>%
  mutate(

    party_num =
      suppressWarnings(as.numeric(partyid)),

    party_factor = case_when(
      party_num == 0 ~ "Strong Democrat",
      party_num == 1 ~ "Not very strong Democrat",
      party_num == 2 ~ "Independent, close Democrat",
      party_num == 3 ~ "Independent",
      party_num == 4 ~ "Independent, close Republican",
      party_num == 5 ~ "Not very strong Republican",
      party_num == 6 ~ "Strong Republican",
      party_num == 7 ~ "Other party",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

  party_factor = factor(
  party_factor,
  levels = c(
    "Strong Democrat",
    "Not very strong Democrat",
    "Independent, close Democrat",
    "Independent",
    "Independent, close Republican",
    "Not very strong Republican",
    "Strong Republican",
    "Other party"
  )
),

    major_party = case_when(
      party_num %in% 0:2 ~ "Democrat",
      party_num %in% 4:6 ~ "Republican",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    major_party = factor(
      major_party,
      levels = c("Democrat", "Republican")
    )

  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Convert to long election format
# ------------------------------------------------------------

gss_presidential <- gss_vote %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(
      vote_2004,
      vote_2008,
      vote_2012,
      vote_2016,
      vote_2020,
      vote_2024
    ),
    names_to = "election",
    values_to = "presidential_vote"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    year =
      as.numeric(
        stringr::str_extract(
          election,
          "\\d{4}"
        )
      ),

    vote_type = case_when(
      year == 2024 ~ "Vote intention",
      TRUE ~ "Reported vote"
    )
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Construct the mechanical OUT-PARTY vote measure
# ------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Democrats:
#   Republican vote = 1
#   Democratic vote = 0
#
# Republicans:
#   Democratic vote = 1
#   Republican vote = 0
#
# Independents and third-party voters = NA
#
# This is intentionally mechanical. It does not attempt
# to infer whether a respondent was "really" a defector.

gss_presidential <- gss_presidential %>%
  mutate(

    outparty_vote = case_when(

      major_party == "Democrat" &
        presidential_vote == "Republican" ~ 1,

      major_party == "Democrat" &
        presidential_vote == "Democratic" ~ 0,

      major_party == "Republican" &
        presidential_vote == "Democratic" ~ 1,

      major_party == "Republican" &
        presidential_vote == "Republican" ~ 0,

      TRUE ~ NA_real_

    )

  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. VERIFY EVERYTHING
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Candidate distribution

gss_presidential %>%
  filter(!is.na(presidential_vote)) %>%
  count(
    year,
    vote_type,
    presidential_vote
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    year,
    presidential_vote
  )


# Out-party voting by election and party

outparty_rates <- gss_presidential %>%
  filter(!is.na(outparty_vote)) %>%
  group_by(
    year,
    vote_type,
    major_party
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    outparty_rate =
      mean(outparty_vote),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(outparty_rates)


# Cross-tabulation is especially important here.

gss_presidential %>%
  filter(!is.na(outparty_vote)) %>%
  count(
    year,
    major_party,
    presidential_vote,
    outparty_vote
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    year,
    major_party,
    presidential_vote
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Build election-level presidential vote data
# ------------------------------------------------------------

presidential_votes <- bind_rows(

  gss_all %>%
    dplyr::transmute(
      respondent_id = row_number(),
      year = 2004,
      party_raw = party,
      presidential_vote =
        classify_pres_vote(pres04, 2004)
    ),

  gss_all %>%
    dplyr::transmute(
      respondent_id = row_number(),
      year = 2008,
      party_raw = party,
      presidential_vote =
        classify_pres_vote(pres08, 2008)
    ),

  gss_all %>%
    dplyr::transmute(
      respondent_id = row_number(),
      year = 2012,
      party_raw = party,
      presidential_vote =
        classify_pres_vote(pres12, 2012)
    ),

  gss_all %>%
    dplyr::transmute(
      respondent_id = row_number(),
      year = 2016,
      party_raw = party,
      presidential_vote =
        classify_pres_vote(pres16, 2016)
    ),

  gss_all %>%
    dplyr::transmute(
      respondent_id = row_number(),
      year = 2020,
      party_raw = party,
      presidential_vote =
        classify_pres_vote(pres20, 2020)
    ),

  gss_all %>%
    dplyr::transmute(
      respondent_id = row_number(),
      year = 2024,
      party_raw = party,
      presidential_vote =
        classify_pres_vote(whovote24, 2024)
    )
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Rebuild the respondent-level variables
# ------------------------------------------------------------

gss_vote <- gss_all %>%
  mutate(
    
    # -------------------------
    # Party identification
    # -------------------------
    party_num = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(partyid)),

    party_factor = case_when(
      party_num == 0 ~ "Strong Democrat",
      party_num == 1 ~ "Not very strong Democrat",
      party_num == 2 ~ "Independent, close Democrat",
      party_num == 3 ~ "Independent",
      party_num == 4 ~ "Independent, close Republican",
      party_num == 5 ~ "Not very strong Republican",
      party_num == 6 ~ "Strong Republican",
      party_num == 7 ~ "Other party",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    party_factor = factor(
      party_factor,
      levels = c(
        "Strong Democrat",
        "Not very strong Democrat",
        "Independent, close Democrat",
        "Independent",
        "Independent, close Republican",
        "Not very strong Republican",
        "Strong Republican",
        "Other party"
      )
    ),

    # Major-party indicator
    major_party = case_when(
      party_num %in% 0:2 ~ "Democrat",
      party_num %in% 4:6 ~ "Republican",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    major_party = factor(
      major_party,
      levels = c("Democrat", "Republican")
    ),

    
    # -------------------------
    # Ideology
    # -------------------------
    polviews_num = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(polviews)),

    polviews_factor = case_when(
      polviews_num == 1 ~ "Extremely liberal",
      polviews_num == 2 ~ "Liberal",
      polviews_num == 3 ~ "Slightly liberal",
      polviews_num == 4 ~ "Moderate",
      polviews_num == 5 ~ "Slightly conservative",
      polviews_num == 6 ~ "Conservative",
      polviews_num == 7 ~ "Extremely conservative",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    polviews_factor = factor(
      polviews_factor,
      levels = c(
        "Moderate",
        "Extremely liberal",
        "Liberal",
        "Slightly liberal",
        "Slightly conservative",
        "Conservative",
        "Extremely conservative"
      )
    ),


    # -------------------------
    # Work status
    # -------------------------
    wrkstat_num = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(wrkstat)),

    wrkstat_factor = case_when(
      wrkstat_num == 1 ~ "Working full time",
      wrkstat_num == 2 ~ "Working part time",
      wrkstat_num == 3 ~ "With a job, not at work",
      wrkstat_num == 4 ~ "Unemployed / looking for work",
      wrkstat_num == 5 ~ "Retired",
      wrkstat_num == 6 ~ "In school",
      wrkstat_num == 7 ~ "Keeping house",
      wrkstat_num == 8 ~ "Other",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    wrkstat_factor = factor(
      wrkstat_factor,
      levels = c(
        "Working full time",
        "Working part time",
        "With a job, not at work",
        "Unemployed / looking for work",
        "Retired",
        "In school",
        "Keeping house",
        "Other"
      )
    ),


    # -------------------------
    # Sex
    # -------------------------
    sex_num = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(sex)),

    sex_factor = case_when(
      sex_num == 1 ~ "Male",
      sex_num == 2 ~ "Female",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    sex_factor = factor(
      sex_factor,
      levels = c("Male", "Female")
    ),


    # -------------------------
    # Social class
    # -------------------------
    class_num = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(class)),

    social_class_factor = case_when(
      class_num == 1 ~ "Lower class",
      class_num == 2 ~ "Working class",
      class_num == 3 ~ "Middle class",
      class_num == 4 ~ "Upper class",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    social_class_factor = factor(
      social_class_factor,
      levels = c(
        "Working class",
        "Lower class",
        "Middle class",
        "Upper class"
      )
    ),


    # -------------------------
    # Income
    # -------------------------
    realrinc_clean = case_when(
      is.na(realrinc) ~ NA_real_,
      realrinc < 0 ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ as.numeric(realrinc)
    ),

    log_realrinc = log1p(realrinc_clean),


    # -------------------------
    # Personal financial
    # satisfaction
    # -------------------------
    satfin_num = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(satfin)),

    financial_satisfaction = case_when(
      satfin_num == 1 ~ 3,
      satfin_num == 2 ~ 2,
      satfin_num == 3 ~ 1,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Construct the presidential vote variable
# ------------------------------------------------------------
#
# First construct election-specific votes directly on the
# respondent file.
#
# This makes it easy to check each election separately.

gss_vote <- gss_vote %>%
  mutate(

    vote_2004 = classify_pres_vote(pres04, 2004),
    vote_2008 = classify_pres_vote(pres08, 2008),
    vote_2012 = classify_pres_vote(pres12, 2012),
    vote_2016 = classify_pres_vote(pres16, 2016),
    vote_2020 = classify_pres_vote(pres20, 2020),
    vote_2024 = classify_pres_vote(whovote24, 2024)

  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Convert to long election format
# ------------------------------------------------------------

gss_presidential <- gss_vote %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(
      vote_2004,
      vote_2008,
      vote_2012,
      vote_2016,
      vote_2020,
      vote_2024
    ),
    names_to = "election",
    values_to = "presidential_vote"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    year = as.numeric(stringr::str_extract(election, "\\d{4}"))
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Construct OUT-PARTY VOTE
# ------------------------------------------------------------
#
# This is the central behavioral outcome.
#
# Democrat voting Republican = 1
# Republican voting Democrat = 1
#
# Same-party vote = 0
#
# Independents are excluded from the primary outcome.

gss_presidential <- gss_presidential %>%
  mutate(

    outparty_vote = case_when(

      major_party == "Democrat" &
        presidential_vote == "Republican" ~ 1,

      major_party == "Democrat" &
        presidential_vote == "Democratic" ~ 0,

      major_party == "Republican" &
        presidential_vote == "Democratic" ~ 1,

      major_party == "Republican" &
        presidential_vote == "Republican" ~ 0,

      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )

  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 9. VERIFY THE RECODING
# ------------------------------------------------------------

gss_presidential %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(major_party),
                !is.na(presidential_vote)) %>%
  count(
    year,
    major_party,
    presidential_vote
  ) %>%
  arrange(year, major_party, presidential_vote)


# Out-party rates by election and party

outparty_rates <- gss_presidential %>%
  filter(!is.na(outparty_vote)) %>%
  group_by(year, major_party) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    outparty_rate = mean(outparty_vote),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(outparty_rates)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 10. MERGE THE INDUSTRY-YEAR JOB QUALITY MEASURES
# ------------------------------------------------------------
#
# If these variables already exist in gss_all, skip this section.
#
# Otherwise use the industry-year master file.

industry_year_job_quality <- readRDS(
  here::here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "industry_year_job_quality_2000_2024.rds"
  )
)


# Reconstruct the GSS industry classification if needed.

gss_presidential <- gss_presidential %>%
  mutate(
    indus10_num = suppressWarnings(as.integer(indus10)),

    industry_bls17 = case_when(
      indus10_num == 770 ~ "Construction",
      indus10_num >= 1070 & indus10_num <= 3990 ~ "Manufacturing",
      indus10_num >= 4070 & indus10_num <= 4590 ~ "Wholesale trade",
      indus10_num >= 4670 & indus10_num <= 5790 ~ "Retail trade",
      indus10_num >= 6070 & indus10_num <= 6390 ~
        "Transportation and warehousing",
      indus10_num >= 6470 & indus10_num <= 6780 ~ "Information",
      indus10_num >= 6870 & indus10_num <= 6990 ~
        "Finance and insurance",
      indus10_num >= 7070 & indus10_num <= 7190 ~
        "Real estate and rental and leasing",
      indus10_num >= 7270 & indus10_num <= 7490 ~
        "Professional, scientific, and technical services",
      indus10_num >= 7570 & indus10_num <= 7790 ~
        "Administrative and support and waste management",
      indus10_num >= 7860 & indus10_num <= 7890 ~
        "Educational services",
      indus10_num >= 7970 & indus10_num <= 8470 ~
        "Health care and social assistance",
      indus10_num >= 8560 & indus10_num <= 8690 ~
        "Leisure and hospitality",
      indus10_num >= 8770 & indus10_num <= 9290 ~
        "Other services",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    industry_common = industry_bls17
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 11. Create / merge the primary JQI measures
# ------------------------------------------------------------

job_quality_primary <- industry_year_job_quality %>%
  mutate(
    z_wage_premium =
      as.numeric(scale(wage_premium)),

    z_ecec_wage =
      as.numeric(scale(wage_cost_per_hour)),

    z_benefits =
      as.numeric(scale(benefits_nonrequired)),

    z_earnings_stability =
      as.numeric(scale(-earnings_volatility)),

    compensation =
      rowMeans(
        cbind(
          z_wage_premium,
          z_ecec_wage
        ),
        na.rm = FALSE
      ),

    benefits = z_benefits,

    earnings_stability =
      z_earnings_stability,

    jqi_primary =
      rowMeans(
        cbind(
          compensation,
          benefits,
          earnings_stability
        ),
        na.rm = FALSE
      ),

    jqi_primary_z =
      as.numeric(scale(jqi_primary))
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    year,
    industry_common,
    compensation,
    benefits,
    earnings_stability,
    jqi_primary,
    jqi_primary_z
  )


# Merge

gss_presidential <- gss_presidential %>%
  left_join(
    job_quality_primary,
    by = c("year", "industry_common")
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 12. Check JQI coverage by election
# ------------------------------------------------------------

gss_presidential %>%
  filter(!is.na(outparty_vote)) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    n_jqi = sum(!is.na(jqi_primary)),
    pct_jqi = mean(!is.na(jqi_primary)) * 100,
    .groups = "drop"
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# ADD EXISTING ANALYTIC VARIABLES
# ------------------------------------------------------------

gss_presidential <- gss_presidential %>%
  mutate(

    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # Employment status
    # ----------------------------------------------------------

    wrkstat_num =
      suppressWarnings(as.numeric(wrkstat)),

    wrkstat_factor = case_when(
      wrkstat_num == 1 ~ "Working full time",
      wrkstat_num == 2 ~ "Working part time",
      wrkstat_num == 3 ~ "With a job, not at work",
      wrkstat_num == 4 ~ "Unemployed / looking for work",
      wrkstat_num == 5 ~ "Retired",
      wrkstat_num == 6 ~ "In school",
      wrkstat_num == 7 ~ "Keeping house",
      wrkstat_num == 8 ~ "Other",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    wrkstat_factor = factor(
      wrkstat_factor,
      levels = c(
        "Working full time",
        "Working part time",
        "With a job, not at work",
        "Unemployed / looking for work",
        "Retired",
        "In school",
        "Keeping house",
        "Other"
      )
    ),


    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # Social class
    # ----------------------------------------------------------

    class_num =
      suppressWarnings(as.numeric(class)),

    social_class_factor = case_when(
      class_num == 1 ~ "Lower class",
      class_num == 2 ~ "Working class",
      class_num == 3 ~ "Middle class",
      class_num == 4 ~ "Upper class",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    social_class_factor = factor(
      social_class_factor,
      levels = c(
        "Working class",
        "Lower class",
        "Middle class",
        "Upper class"
      )
    ),


    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # Income
    # ----------------------------------------------------------

    realrinc_clean = case_when(
      is.na(realrinc) ~ NA_real_,
      realrinc < 0 ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ as.numeric(realrinc)
    ),

    log_realrinc =
      log1p(realrinc_clean),


    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # Personal financial satisfaction
    # ----------------------------------------------------------

    satfin_num =
      suppressWarnings(as.numeric(satfin)),

    financial_satisfaction = case_when(
      satfin_num == 1 ~ 3,
      satfin_num == 2 ~ 2,
      satfin_num == 3 ~ 1,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )

  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# VERIFY VARIABLES NOW EXIST
# ------------------------------------------------------------

gss_presidential %>%
  dplyr::select(
    year,
    outparty_vote,
    wrkstat_factor,
    social_class_factor,
    log_realrinc,
    financial_satisfaction,
    compensation,
    benefits,
    earnings_stability,
    jqi_primary,
    prestg10
  ) %>%
  glimpse()

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 13. PRIMARY MODEL SET
# ------------------------------------------------------------
#
# These are pooled models across elections.
#
# Election-year fixed effects are included because the
# political environment differs enormously across elections.
#
# The five models mirror the political-attitudes analysis.

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# PRIMARY PRESIDENTIAL VOTE MODELS
# ------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Each model uses its own complete-case sample.
#
# This avoids unnecessarily restricting the simpler models
# because of missingness in variables only used in M5.
#
# The function also checks categorical variables for
# sufficient variation before fitting.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

run_vote_models <- function(data) {

  formulas <- list(

    M1_employment =
      outparty_vote ~
      wrkstat_factor +
      factor(year),

    M2_class =
      outparty_vote ~
      wrkstat_factor +
      social_class_factor +
      factor(year),

    M3_JQI =
      outparty_vote ~
      wrkstat_factor +
      compensation +
      benefits +
      earnings_stability +
      factor(year),

    M4_class_JQI =
      outparty_vote ~
      wrkstat_factor +
      social_class_factor +
      compensation +
      benefits +
      earnings_stability +
      factor(year),

    M5_full =
      outparty_vote ~
      wrkstat_factor +
      social_class_factor +
      compensation +
      benefits +
      earnings_stability +
      prestg10 +
      log_realrinc +
      financial_satisfaction +
      factor(year)
  )


  models <- list()


  for (model_name in names(formulas)) {

    f <- formulas[[model_name]]

    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Variables required by this particular model
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    model_vars <- all.vars(f)

    d <- data %>%
      filter(
        if_all(
          all_of(model_vars),
          ~ !is.na(.x)
        )
      ) %>%
      droplevels()


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Basic sample-size check
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    if (nrow(d) < 100) {

      message(
        model_name,
        ": fewer than 100 complete cases. Skipping."
      )

      next
    }


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Check outcome variation
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    if (dplyr::n_distinct(d$outparty_vote) < 2) {

      message(
        model_name,
        ": outcome has fewer than two levels. Skipping."
      )

      next
    }


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Check factor variation
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    factor_vars <- model_vars[
      model_vars %in%
        names(d)[vapply(
          d,
          is.factor,
          logical(1)
        )]
    ]


    factor_check <- tibble(
      variable = factor_vars,
      n_levels = vapply(
        d[factor_vars],
        function(x)
          nlevels(droplevels(x)),
        integer(1)
      )
    )


    bad_factors <- factor_check %>%
      filter(n_levels < 2)


    if (nrow(bad_factors) > 0) {

      message(
        "\n",
        model_name,
        " has factor(s) with fewer than two levels:\n"
      )

      print(bad_factors)

      message(
        "\nLevels observed in the model sample:\n"
      )

      for (v in bad_factors$variable) {

        print(
          d %>%
            count(.data[[v]], .drop = FALSE)
        )

      }

      message(
        "\nSkipping ",
        model_name,
        "."
      )

      next
    }


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Fit model
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    models[[model_name]] <-
      glm(
        f,
        data = d,
        family = binomial(link = "logit")
      )


    # Store sample size
    attr(
      models[[model_name]],
      "analysis_n"
    ) <- nrow(d)

  }


  models
}

extract_vote_terms <- function(model, model_name) {

  broom::tidy(model) %>%
    mutate(
      model = model_name,
      odds_ratio = exp(estimate),
      conf_low = exp(estimate - 1.96 * std.error),
      conf_high = exp(estimate + 1.96 * std.error)
    ) %>%
    filter(
      term %in% c(
        "compensation",
        "benefits",
        "earnings_stability",
        "prestige",
        "log_realrinc",
        "financial_satisfaction"
      )
    )
}

# 16. Incremental model comparisons
# ------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Because the models use the same common sample, LR tests
# can be used to ask whether JQI adds information.

vote_lr_tests <- tibble(

  comparison = c(
    "M1 vs M2: social class beyond employment status",
    "M1 vs M3: JQI beyond employment status",
    "M2 vs M4: JQI beyond employment status + class",
    "M4 vs M5: prestige + income + financial satisfaction"
  ),

  lr_statistic = c(
    2 * (logLik(vote_models$M2) -
           logLik(vote_models$M1)),

    2 * (logLik(vote_models$M3) -
           logLik(vote_models$M1)),

    2 * (logLik(vote_models$M4) -
           logLik(vote_models$M2)),

    2 * (logLik(vote_models$M5) -
           logLik(vote_models$M4))
  ),

  df = c(
    attr(logLik(vote_models$M2), "df") -
      attr(logLik(vote_models$M1), "df"),

    attr(logLik(vote_models$M3), "df") -
      attr(logLik(vote_models$M1), "df"),

    attr(logLik(vote_models$M4), "df") -
      attr(logLik(vote_models$M2), "df"),

    attr(logLik(vote_models$M5), "df") -
      attr(logLik(vote_models$M4), "df")
  )

) %>%
  mutate(
    p_value = pchisq(
      lr_statistic,
      df = df,
      lower.tail = FALSE
    )
  )

print(vote_lr_tests)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 17. YEAR-SPECIFIC MODELS
# ------------------------------------------------------------
#
# This is important because the substantive question is
# explicitly about change over time.
#
# We first estimate the disaggregated JQI model separately
# for every election.

run_year_vote_models <- function(data) {

  years <- sort(unique(data$year))

  results <- list()

  for (yr in years) {

    d <- data %>%
      filter(
        year == yr,
        !is.na(outparty_vote)
      )

    if (nrow(d) < 100) {
      next
    }

    f <- outparty_vote ~
      wrkstat_factor +
      social_class_factor +
      compensation +
      benefits +
      earnings_stability

    vars <- all.vars(f)

    d_complete <- d %>%
      filter(
        if_all(
          all_of(vars),
          ~ !is.na(.x)
        )
      ) %>%
      droplevels()

    if (nrow(d_complete) < 100) {
      next
    }

    fit <- glm(
      f,
      data = d_complete,
      family = binomial(link = "logit")
    )

    results[[as.character(yr)]] <-
      broom::tidy(fit) %>%
      filter(
        term %in% c(
          "compensation",
          "benefits",
          "earnings_stability"
        )
      ) %>%
      mutate(
        year = yr,
        n = nrow(d_complete),
        odds_ratio = exp(estimate),
        conf_low =
          exp(estimate - 1.96 * std.error),
        conf_high =
          exp(estimate + 1.96 * std.error)
      )
  }

  bind_rows(results)
}


vote_year_results <-
  run_year_vote_models(gss_presidential)

print(vote_year_results)

    if (nrow(d_complete) < 100) {

    fit <- glm(

      ) %>%

}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 19. ECONOMIC DISPOSSESSION / PARTY DEFECTION
# ------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Now we move from "what predicts out-party voting?"
# to the more specific question:
#
# Does economic disadvantage make people more likely
# to vote against their own party?
#
# First, define economically disadvantaged indicators.
#
# We use quartiles so that the measures are comparable and
# do not impose arbitrary unit differences across measures.

gss_presidential <- gss_presidential %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  mutate(

    income_q = ntile(
      log_realrinc,
      4
    ),

    financial_q = ntile(
      financial_satisfaction,
      4
    ),

    compensation_q = ntile(
      compensation,
      4
    ),

    benefits_q = ntile(
      benefits,
      4
    ),

    earnings_stability_q = ntile(
      earnings_stability,
      4
    ),

    jqi_q = ntile(
      jqi_primary,
      4
    ),

    prestige_q = ntile(
      prestg10,
      4
    )

  ) %>%
  ungroup()


# Direction of dispossession:
#
# Lower income = greater dispossession
# Lower financial satisfaction = greater dispossession
# Lower compensation = greater dispossession
# Lower benefits = greater dispossession
# Lower JQI = greater dispossession
# Lower prestige = greater dispossession
#
# For earnings stability, "dispossession" is conceptually
# less straightforward, so we keep it separate rather than
# arbitrarily treating instability as equivalent to low
# compensation.


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 20. Basic dispossession → out-party vote models
# ------------------------------------------------------------

dispossession_models <- list(

  income =
    glm(
      outparty_vote ~
        factor(income_q) +
        party_factor +
        polviews_factor +
        factor(year),
      data = gss_presidential,
      family = binomial,
      na.action = na.omit
    ),

  financial_satisfaction =
    glm(
      outparty_vote ~
        factor(financial_q) +
        party_factor +
        polviews_factor +
        factor(year),
      data = gss_presidential,
      family = binomial,
      na.action = na.omit
    ),

  compensation =
    glm(
      outparty_vote ~
        factor(compensation_q) +
        party_factor +
        polviews_factor +
        factor(year),
      data = gss_presidential,
      family = binomial,
      na.action = na.omit
    ),

  benefits =
    glm(
      outparty_vote ~
        factor(benefits_q) +
        party_factor +
        polviews_factor +
        factor(year),
      data = gss_presidential,
      family = binomial,
      na.action = na.omit
    ),

  jqi =
    glm(
      outparty_vote ~
        factor(jqi_q) +
        party_factor +
        polviews_factor +
        factor(year),
      data = gss_presidential,
      family = binomial,
      na.action = na.omit
    ),

  prestige =
    glm(
      outparty_vote ~
        factor(prestige_q) +
        party_factor +
        polviews_factor +
        factor(year),
      data = gss_presidential,
      family = binomial,
      na.action = na.omit
    )
)


# Odds ratios

dispossession_results <- purrr::map2_dfr(
  dispossession_models,
  names(dispossession_models),
  ~ broom::tidy(.x) %>%
    mutate(
      measure = .y,
      odds_ratio = exp(estimate),
      conf_low =
        exp(estimate - 1.96 * std.error),
      conf_high =
        exp(estimate + 1.96 * std.error)
    )
)

print(dispossession_results)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 21. THE KEY "ECONOMIC NIHILISM" MODEL
# ------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Here we test whether economic position changes the
# predictive power of PARTY IDENTIFICATION.
#
# We use party strength as a categorical measure rather
# than treating party as a linear 0-6 scale.
#
# The interaction is the key:
#
# economic_dispossession × party
#
# If economic deprivation weakens partisan voting,
# the relationship between party identification and vote
# should be weaker among economically dispossessed respondents.

nihilism_income <- glm(
  outparty_vote ~
    party_factor * factor(income_q) +
    polviews_factor +
    factor(year),
  data = gss_presidential,
  family = binomial,
  na.action = na.omit
)

nihilism_financial <- glm(
  outparty_vote ~
    party_factor * factor(financial_q) +
    polviews_factor +
    factor(year),
  data = gss_presidential,
  family = binomial,
  na.action = na.omit
)

nihilism_compensation <- glm(
  outparty_vote ~
    party_factor * factor(compensation_q) +
    polviews_factor +
    factor(year),
  data = gss_presidential,
  family = binomial,
  na.action = na.omit
)

nihilism_benefits <- glm(
  outparty_vote ~
    party_factor * factor(benefits_q) +
    polviews_factor +
    factor(year),
  data = gss_presidential,
  family = binomial,
  na.action = na.omit
)

nihilism_jqi <- glm(
  outparty_vote ~
    party_factor * factor(jqi_q) +
    polviews_factor +
    factor(year),
  data = gss_presidential,
  family = binomial,
  na.action = na.omit
)

nihilism_prestige <- glm(
  outparty_vote ~
    party_factor * factor(prestige_q) +
    polviews_factor +
    factor(year),
  data = gss_presidential,
  family = binomial,
  na.action = na.omit
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 22. Test whether the PARTY interactions matter jointly
# ------------------------------------------------------------

party_interaction_tests <- tibble(

  measure = c(
    "Income",
    "Financial satisfaction",
    "Compensation",
    "Benefits",
    "Primary JQI",
    "Prestige"
  ),

  p_value = c(

    anova(
      update(
        nihilism_income,
        . ~ . -
          party_factor:factor(income_q)
      ),
      nihilism_income,
      test = "Chisq"
    )$`Pr(>Chi)`[2],

    anova(
      update(
        nihilism_financial,
        . ~ . -
          party_factor:factor(financial_q)
      ),
      nihilism_financial,
      test = "Chisq"
    )$`Pr(>Chi)`[2],

    anova(
      update(
        nihilism_compensation,
        . ~ . -
          party_factor:factor(compensation_q)
      ),
      nihilism_compensation,
      test = "Chisq"
    )$`Pr(>Chi)`[2],

    anova(
      update(
        nihilism_benefits,
        . ~ . -
          party_factor:factor(benefits_q)
      ),
      nihilism_benefits,
      test = "Chisq"
    )$`Pr(>Chi)`[2],

    anova(
      update(
        nihilism_jqi,
        . ~ . -
          party_factor:factor(jqi_q)
      ),
      nihilism_jqi,
      test = "Chisq"
    )$`Pr(>Chi)`[2],

    anova(
      update(
        nihilism_prestige,
        . ~ . -
          party_factor:factor(prestige_q)
      ),
      nihilism_prestige,
      test = "Chisq"
    )$`Pr(>Chi)`[2]

  )
)

print(party_interaction_tests)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 25. THE STRONGER OVER-TIME NIHILISM TEST
# ------------------------------------------------------------
#
# The previous models ask whether economic conditions
# weaken the predictive power of party/ideology.
#
# Now ask whether that weakening itself has become stronger
# across elections.
#
# This is the central three-way interaction:
#
# Party × Economic Position × Year
#
# If economic nihilism has increased over time, the
# interaction should be detectable here.

nihilism_time_income <- glm(
  outparty_vote ~
    party_factor *
    factor(income_q) *
    factor(year) +
    polviews_factor,
  data = gss_presidential,
  family = binomial,
  na.action = na.omit
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 26. Formal three-way tests
# ------------------------------------------------------------

three_way_test <- function(model, interaction_term) {

  reduced_formula <- update(
    formula(model),
    paste(
      ". ~ . -",
      interaction_term
    ) %>%
      as.formula()
  )

  reduced <- glm(
    reduced_formula,
    data = model$data,
    family = binomial
  )

  anova(
    reduced,
    model,
    test = "Chisq"
  )
}


# Because the exact interaction names can be cumbersome,
# use likelihood-ratio comparisons directly.

test_three_way <- function(full_model,
                           reduced_formula,
                           data) {

  reduced_model <- glm(
    reduced_formula,
    data = data,
    family = binomial
  )

  test <- anova(
    reduced_model,
    full_model,
    test = "Chisq"
  )

  tibble(
    lr_statistic = test$Deviance[2],
    df = test$Df[2],
    p_value = test$`Pr(>Chi)`[2]
  )
}


# Income
income_three_way <- test_three_way(
  nihilism_time_income,
  outparty_vote ~
    party_factor * factor(income_q) +
    party_factor * factor(year) +

    polviews_factor,
  gss_presidential
)

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# FUNCTION TO TEST THE THREE-WAY INTERACTION
# ---------------------------------------------------------

test_three_way <- function(full_model, reduced_model, measure) {

  lr <- anova(
    reduced_model,
    full_model,
    test = "LRT"
  )

  tibble(
    measure = measure,
    df = lr$Df[2],
    lr_statistic = lr$Deviance[2],
    p_value = lr$`Pr(>Chi)`[2]
  )
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------

  test_three_way(
    nihilism_income_full,
    nihilism_income_reduced,
    "Income"
  ),

  test_three_way(
    nihilism_financial_full,
    nihilism_financial_reduced,
    "Financial satisfaction"
  ),

  test_three_way(
    nihilism_compensation_full,
    nihilism_compensation_reduced,
    "Compensation"
  ),

  test_three_way(
    nihilism_benefits_full,
    nihilism_benefits_reduced,
    "Benefits"
  ),

  test_three_way(
    nihilism_jqi_full,
    nihilism_jqi_reduced,
    "JQI"
  ),

  test_three_way(
    nihilism_prestige_full,

)

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# PARTY PREDICTIVENESS ACROSS ECONOMIC POSITION
# JQI, 2004–2020
# ---------------------------------------------------------
#
# Question:
# Does the predictive effect of party direction on
# presidential vote become weaker among economically
# disadvantaged respondents over time?
#
# republican_vote:
#   1 = Republican candidate
#   0 = Democratic candidate
#
# party_direction:
#   Democrat
#   Republican
#
# JQI is standardized, so we evaluate the party effect at:
#   - 25th percentile = relatively disadvantaged
#   - 50th percentile = median
#   - 75th percentile = relatively advantaged
# ---------------------------------------------------------


# Estimate the model allowing the JQI × party relationship
# to vary by election year
nihilism_jqi_year_model <- glm(
  republican_vote ~
    party_direction * jqi_z * factor(year),
  data = gss_vote_actual,
  family = binomial(link = "logit")
)


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# Generate prediction grid
# ---------------------------------------------------------

jqi_values <- quantile(
  gss_vote_actual$jqi_z,
  probs = c(.25, .50, .75),
  na.rm = TRUE
)

prediction_grid_jqi <- expand_grid(
  year = c(2004, 2008, 2012, 2016, 2020),
  party_direction = c("Democrat", "Republican"),
  jqi_z = as.numeric(jqi_values)
) %>%
  mutate(
    party_direction = factor(
      party_direction,
      levels = c("Democrat", "Republican")
    ),
    year = factor(
      year,
      levels = c(2004, 2008, 2012, 2016, 2020)
    )
  )


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# Predicted probabilities
# ---------------------------------------------------------

prediction_grid_jqi <- prediction_grid_jqi %>%
  mutate(
    predicted_probability = predict(
      nihilism_jqi_year_model,
      newdata = prediction_grid_jqi,
      type = "response"
    ),

    economic_position = case_when(
      jqi_z == as.numeric(jqi_values[1]) ~ "Low JQI (25th percentile)",
      jqi_z == as.numeric(jqi_values[2]) ~ "Median JQI (50th percentile)",
      jqi_z == as.numeric(jqi_values[3]) ~ "High JQI (75th percentile)"
    )
  )


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# Calculate the party-direction predictive gap
#
# Republican probability minus Democratic probability
# ---------------------------------------------------------

party_predictiveness_jqi <- prediction_grid_jqi %>%
  select(
    year,
    economic_position,
    jqi_z,
    party_direction,
    predicted_probability
  ) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = party_direction,
    values_from = predicted_probability
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    party_direction_gap = Republican - Democrat
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    year,
    jqi_z
  )

print(party_predictiveness_jqi)


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# ECONOMIC NIHILISM: OUT-PARTY VOTING
# JQI, 2004–2020
# ---------------------------------------------------------
#
# Question:
# Are economically disadvantaged partisans increasingly
# willing to vote against their own party?
#
# outparty_vote:
#   1 = voted against own major party
#   0 = voted for own major party
#
# party_direction:
#   Democrat
#   Republican
#
# JQI:
#   Higher values = better objective job quality
#
# Primary focus:
#   respondents at the 25th percentile of JQI
# ---------------------------------------------------------


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Create the JQI threshold
# ---------------------------------------------------------

jqi_low <- quantile(
  gss_vote_actual$jqi_z,
  probs = .25,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

jqi_low


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Estimate the model
# ---------------------------------------------------------
#
# We allow the relationship between JQI and out-party
# voting to differ by party and election year.
# ---------------------------------------------------------

nihilism_outparty_jqi <- glm(
  outparty_vote ~
    party_direction * jqi_z * factor(year),
  data = gss_vote_actual,
  family = binomial(link = "logit")
)


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Create prediction grid
# ---------------------------------------------------------

outparty_prediction_grid <- expand_grid(
  year = c(2004, 2008, 2012, 2016, 2020),
  party_direction = c("Democrat", "Republican"),
  jqi_z = jqi_low
) %>%
  mutate(
    party_direction = factor(
      party_direction,
      levels = c("Democrat", "Republican")
    ),

    year = factor(
      year,
      levels = c(2004, 2008, 2012, 2016, 2020)
    )
  )


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Predicted probability of voting against one's party
# ---------------------------------------------------------

outparty_prediction_grid <- outparty_prediction_grid %>%
  mutate(
    predicted_outparty_probability = predict(
      nihilism_outparty_jqi,
      newdata = outparty_prediction_grid,
      type = "response"
    )
  )

print(outparty_prediction_grid)


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Put Democrats and Republicans side-by-side
# ---------------------------------------------------------

outparty_by_party <- outparty_prediction_grid %>%
  select(
    year,
    party_direction,
    predicted_outparty_probability
  ) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = party_direction,
    values_from = predicted_outparty_probability
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Democrat_minus_Republican =
      Democrat - Republican
  )

print(outparty_by_party)


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# FORMAL TEST: OUT-PARTY VOTING AMONG LOW-JQI PARTISANS
# 2004–2020
# ---------------------------------------------------------

# Define economically disadvantaged respondents as those
# at or below the 25th percentile of JQI.

gss_low_jqi <- gss_vote_actual %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(jqi_z),
    jqi_z <= jqi_low,
    !is.na(outparty_vote),
    !is.na(party_direction)
  )


# Model allowing out-party voting to vary by party and year
low_jqi_outparty_model <- glm(
  outparty_vote ~
    party_direction * factor(year),
  data = gss_low_jqi,
  family = binomial(link = "logit")
)

summary(low_jqi_outparty_model)


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# Joint test of whether out-party voting changes across
# elections differently for Democrats and Republicans
# ---------------------------------------------------------

low_jqi_outparty_reduced <- glm(
  outparty_vote ~
    party_direction +
    factor(year),
  data = gss_low_jqi,
  family = binomial(link = "logit")
)

anova(
  low_jqi_outparty_reduced,
  low_jqi_outparty_model,
  test = "LRT"
)
```
